title: The Great Samosa Startup
synopsis: A Pune office team launches a samosa subscription and discovers the dangers of corporate jargon.

chapters.title: The Pitch Deck
paragraphs: Rohit had spent six months at a startup in Pune and had learned one powerful truth: anything sounded expensive when followed by the word ecosystem. He proposed a 'distributed potato-delivery ecosystem' to his colleagues. Priya asked whether he meant selling samosas.

'Not selling,' Rohit corrected her. 'Disrupting evening hunger.' Their manager approved a pilot, provided it cost no more than the office tea budget. Rohit immediately made a thirty-slide presentation.

chapters.title: The Beta Test
paragraphs: The first customer was the receptionist, who ordered two samosas without chutney. Rohit's app insisted she select a 'chutney journey' before checkout. Priya bypassed the form and wrote the order on paper.

By four o'clock the app had received twenty-seven orders, including one from the office printer. Rohit called it strong machine adoption. Priya discovered that someone had used the printer's name to test the form.

chapters.title: The Influencer Incident
paragraphs: To attract attention, Rohit invited a food influencer to the office. Unfortunately, he had confused her account with a page dedicated to antique pressure cookers. The guest arrived expecting to review a 1970s cooker and was disappointed by the absence of steam valves.

The cook from the canteen rescued the afternoon by offering her a hot samosa. She posted a review anyway: 'Excellent snack. Very poor pressure cooker.' The video attracted thousands of curious viewers.

chapters.title: The Chutney Crisis
paragraphs: The sudden demand overwhelmed Rohit's spreadsheet. Green chutney went to the accounting department, tamarind chutney went to a meeting about cybersecurity, and the managing director received a receipt reading 'One potato, enterprise edition.'

Priya stopped taking orders for ten minutes and asked the canteen staff what capacity they could actually handle. The answer was forty samosas, not four hundred. Rohit reluctantly removed the 'infinite scalability' claim from the website.

chapters.title: The Investor Meeting
paragraphs: A local investor agreed to hear their idea. Rohit arrived with charts showing exponential growth. The investor asked a single question: 'Are the samosas good?' Rohit had not included taste in the metrics.

Priya brought a fresh plate from the canteen. The investor ate one, asked for another and suggested they begin with a simple pre-order system. 'A business is not a presentation,' she said, brushing crumbs from her notebook.

chapters.title: An Honest Menu
paragraphs: The new ordering page had three options, clear prices and a daily limit. Customers liked knowing when the samosas would arrive. The canteen staff received proper credit and a share of the profits.
Rohit kept one slide from his original deck. It read 'Vision: Transform the future of snacking.' Priya added a handwritten note beneath it: 'First, remember the chutney.'
